app.title: Manmen
app.description: Power settings, manuals, processes, and Docker cleanup from a GUI

pmset.title: Power settings (pmset)
pmset.description: Choose a power source, a setting, and a value. Administrator privileges are required.
pmset.adminNote: macOS shows an administrator authentication dialog on execute. Your password is never stored by the app.
pmset.remember: Skip password prompts (while the app is running)
pmset.rememberNote: Enter your password only once; subsequent runs need no password while the app is open. The password is never stored. After quitting, the credential expires with the normal timeout (about 5 minutes).
pmset.empty: Pick a setting and value, then run to see the result here.

pmsetSettings.proximitywake: wake when a nearby device is close
pmsetSettings.acwake: wake when the power source changes
pmsetSettings.destroyfvkeyonstandby: destroy the FileVault key on standby

man.title: Manual pages (man)
man.description: Pick a command from the list to display its manual page. No administrator privileges needed.
man.empty: Click a command in the list to show its manual here.

manAbout.title: About this command
manAbout.man: The standard macOS command for displaying online manuals (man man: display online manual documentation pages). Give it a command name to see its description, options, and examples.
manAbout.usage: Pick a command from the list above (e.g. pmset, caffeinate, launchctl) and press Show. Names not in the list (options, etc.) are rejected.

top.title: Process monitor (top)
top.description: Take a CPU / memory usage snapshot. No administrator privileges needed.
top.userInvalid: User names may contain only letters, digits, and . _ -
top.pidsInvalid: Enter up to 16 process IDs as integers separated by commas
top.statsHint: Leave everything unchecked to use top's default columns. Up to 16 columns.
top.note: Interactive mode is not supported, so this takes a one-shot snapshot in logging mode (-l 1). Treat %CPU in the first sample as approximate. Delay (-s) and repeated samples are not available.
top.hintSecondary: Breaks ties when the first key is equal. Leave blank to skip it.
top.hintCount: How many processes to list, from 1 to 100.
top.hintUser: Shows only processes owned by this user. Blank means everyone.
top.hintPids: Shows only these processes. Separate several IDs with commas.
top.hintNcols: Width of the log output. Too narrow drops columns from the table. Blank keeps top's default.
top.hintFrameworks: Leaves shared-library (framework) statistics out of the summary.
top.hintMemoryMap: Inspects each process's memory so sizes such as resident memory are numbers instead of N/A.
top.hintSwap: Adds swap, purgeable memory, and disk and network totals to the summary.
top.empty: Pick options and run to see the process list here.

topOrderHelp.default: Largest values first. This is top's default, passed as -o cpu with no prefix.
topOrderHelp.+: Smallest values first. The command becomes -o +cpu.
topOrderHelp.-: Largest values first, written explicitly as -o -cpu.

topModeHelp.n: CPU is a share since the previous sample. A single snapshot has little delta, so treat %CPU as approximate.
topModeHelp.a: Counts CPU and time cumulatively since top started.
topModeHelp.d: Counts only the change since the previous sample. Memory-map reporting is off unless you turn it on.

topHelp.pid: The number that identifies the process.
topHelp.command: The name of the running program.
topHelp.cpu: How much of the CPU the process is using.
topHelp.cpu_me: CPU time charged to this process by others.
topHelp.cpu_others: CPU time this process charged to others.
topHelp.csw: How many times the CPU switched to or from this process.
topHelp.time: Total CPU time used so far.
topHelp.threads: How many threads the process has.
topHelp.ports: How many Mach ports it holds.
topHelp.mregion: How many memory regions it has.
topHelp.mem: Physical memory the process is using.
topHelp.rprvt: Resident memory not shared with other processes.
topHelp.purg: Memory that can be discarded under pressure.
topHelp.vsize: Total virtual memory assigned to the process.
topHelp.vprvt: Address space private to the process.
topHelp.kprvt: Private memory held in the kernel.
topHelp.kshrd: Shared memory held in the kernel.
topHelp.pgrp: The process group this process belongs to.
topHelp.ppid: The process ID of the parent that started it.
topHelp.state: Current state, such as running or sleeping.
topHelp.uid: Numeric user ID of the owner.
topHelp.wq: Workqueue total and how many are running.
topHelp.faults: Times memory had to be fetched in (page faults).
topHelp.cow: Times memory was copied because it was written.
topHelp.pageins: Pages read from disk into memory.
topHelp.boosts: Times the process was temporarily raised in priority.
topHelp.cycles: CPU cycles spent running those instructions.
topHelp.jetpri: Jetsam priority: how likely the process is to be quit when memory is low.

topAbout.title: About this command
topAbout.top: The standard macOS command for displaying sorted process information (man top: display sorted information about processes). Sorting uses -o, the secondary key uses -O, and the count uses -n.
topAbout.usage: Choose sort, filters, counting, and columns, then press Snapshot. Only a single `top -l 1` run is executed. Delay (-s), interactive mode, and unknown keys are not accepted.

docker.title: Docker management (docker)
docker.description: Inspect containers, images, networks, volumes, disk usage, and build cache. No administrator privileges needed. All parsed from --format json into tables.
docker.pruneSummary: Open only when needed (pruning cannot be undone)
docker.name: Builder name
docker.nameInvalid: Builder names may contain only letters, digits, and . _ -
docker.hintName: Leave blank to inspect the current builder. Names starting with - are rejected.
docker.note: Pruning cannot be undone. Without --all only dangling cache is removed.
docker.hintForce: Remove without confirmation (-f). Turning it off may fail on the confirmation prompt.
docker.hintAll: Remove all unused cache (--all). Off means dangling cache only.
docker.noOptions: This subcommand takes no options. Just run it.
docker.empty: Pick a subcommand and run to see the result here.

dockerAbout.title: About this command
dockerAbout.docker: Inspects Docker state and prunes build cache (container ls -a / image ls / network ls / volume ls / system df / info / builder du, ls, inspect, version, prune). Reads parse --format json into tables and change nothing. Only prune deletes (-f / --all).
dockerAbout.usage: Pick a subcommand and press Run to inspect. Keep -f on and press Prune to delete. Turn --all on only to free a lot of space.

about.title: About this command
about.pmset: The standard macOS command for manipulating power management settings (man pmset: manipulate power management settings). It manages idle sleep timing, wake on network access, automatic restart on power loss, and more. Administrator (root) privileges are required to change settings.
about.sudo: sudo — run with administrator privileges. Required because changing pmset settings must be done as root.
about.scopes: -a applies to every power source. -b is battery only, -c is the power adapter only, and -u is UPS only.
about.value: setting and value — the chosen option and its value. Only 0/1, minutes (0–1440), or hibernatemode (0 / 3 / 25) are accepted. Immediate actions such as schedule or sleepnow are not available.
about.disablesleep: disablesleep — enable / disable system sleep (0 / 1). Shown as SleepDisabled in `pmset -g` output.
about.on: ON (1) — the system no longer sleeps automatically. Use for long tasks or presentations. Power usage and heat increase, so switch back OFF when done.
about.off: OFF (0) — return to normal sleep behavior. The system then sleeps according to timer settings such as sleep.

ui.stale: Options changed — run again to refresh

dockerSubHelp.prune: Delete build cache. Cannot be undone.
dockerSubHelp.containers: List containers (docker container ls -a), including stopped (read-only).
dockerSubHelp.sysdf: Show per-type disk usage (docker system df) (read-only).
